The best match for the farm's future climate in the 2050s under high emissions is Gilliam County, OR, with a match quality of good and 5 out of 8 climate models agreeing. A lower sigma score means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate; the top matches have a sigma of 1.1 to 1.22, which falls into the good range of 1 to 2.

Out of 5 matching areas checked, 0 use the field's current rotation of a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, winter wheat. The rotations used at the matching places are winter wheat to fallow, covering 95 percent of analog cropland across 5 areas, and continuous winter wheat, covering 1 percent across 0 areas.

Comparing the field to the best match, days above 32 degrees C per year are 32 at the field today and 32 at the match today. Frost-free days are 164 at the field today and 192 at the match today. Afternoon ground temperature in June is 41.1 degrees C at the field today and 39.7 degrees C at the match today. Afternoon ground temperature in July and August is 46.4 degrees C at the field today and 46.5 degrees C at the match today. Driest-month soil water in September is 17.8 percent at the field today and 19.2 percent at the match today.

Looking ahead to the 2050s under high emissions, temperatures and precipitation will shift across the year. These results are based on 3351 farmland cells at approximately 4 kilometers using the Cropland Data Layer.
